title: MS2CAST: A Video Anomaly Detection Framework via Multi-Scale Spatial Cross-Attention and Efficient Spatiotemporal Networks

problem.summary: Video anomaly detection (VAD) is a challenging task for surveillance systems due to the scarcity and diversity of anomalous events.
statements: Video anomaly detection (VAD) is a challenging task for surveillance systems due to the scarcity and diversity of anomalous events.
While semi-supervised VAD approaches have advanced the field, many rely on computationally intensive optical flow networks to capture motion dynamics.
Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are also widely used for spatial encoding, but their effective receptive field is highly local.

background.summary: Beyond traditional approaches [1], [2] recent advances in deep learning have revolutionized VAD by defining different learning tasks that are based on various supervision signals.

In general, multi-modal VAD frameworks utilize either traditional optical flow algorithms [30], [31], [32] or deep pretrained optical flow networks [16], [33], [34].

solution.summary: One module (SwinLSTM) incorporates a Swin Transformer, while the other (VMRNN) integrates Vision Mamba blocks.
solution.approach: One module (SwinLSTM) incorporates a Swin Transformer, while the other (VMRNN) integrates Vision Mamba blocks.
components: Our objective function combines L1 loss, Gradient Difference Loss (GDL), and Multi-Scale Structural Similarity Index Measure (MS-SSIM) to ensure pixel-wise accuracy, sharpness, and structural integrity.

Evaluations across the UCSD Ped2, CUHK Avenue, and ShanghaiTech datasets demonstrate frame-level Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) Area Under the Curve (AUC) scores that are competitive with top-tier techniques while maintaining a peak GPU memory usage of under 1 GB.
Keywords: Video anomaly detection; Multi-scale cross-attention; VMamba; Vision transformers; MS-SSIM 1.

evidence.quote: One module (SwinLSTM) incorporates a Swin Transformer, while the other (VMRNN) integrates Vision Mamba blocks.

Our objective function combines L1 loss, Gradient Difference Loss (GDL), and Multi-Scale Structural Similarity Index Measure (MS-SSIM) to ensure pixel-wise accuracy, sharpness, and structural integrity.

experiments.summary: Following established protocols in VAD research [9], we use the frame-level Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) Area Under the Curve (AUC) to quantitatively evaluate our proposed framework.

evidence.quote: Following established protocols in VAD research [9], we use the frame-level Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) Area Under the Curve (AUC) to quantitatively evaluate our proposed framework.
The MS2CAST framework is implemented in PyTorch and evaluated on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU (40 GB VRAM).

limitations.summary: While the anomaly scoring currently exhibits dataset-dependent sensitivity to the hyperparameter 𝑤, future work will focus on exploring alternative metrics and formulating a unified, parameter-free anomaly score function.
